problems: The blind guess (umbrella or canopy over a stick figure) does not match the intended subject. The drawing reads as a kite with a tail, which only appears in the second alternative, so the figure is not recognisable as a kite at a glance.
The kite body is very small and compressed (roughly x 175-310, y 240-290). The diamond shape is hard to read, and the figure looks more like a wedge or arrow.
The crown and left-wing-tip labels overlap each other near (180-300, 230-250), and several labels are cut off ('wh', 'th', 'b', 'name-stri'). The labels are unreadable.
The pale blue lines run almost exactly alongside the gold lines along the spar, spine and tail. The blue layer looks like a duplicate offset of the gold outline, not an independent silhouette.

Orientation is correct: the crown is at the top, the tail hangs down, and the ribbon and name-strip branch below. The key stars sit near their intended parts (crown, wing tip, lower corner, name-knot, ribbon tip, strip tip).
The cross-spar is not clearly visible. It is a short segment near the crown, so the kite's wing structure does not read well.
output.advice: Enlarge the kite body so the diamond occupies a clear share of the frame, with the crown near the top-centre and the wing tips spread wide. Keep the orientation as it is (crown up, tail down). Make the cross-spar a visibly separate horizontal segment through the crown-to-spine junction at star 93085. Put the pale blue silhouette on its own outline and stop it from tracing the gold lines exactly; offset it or fill it so it reads as a shape. Move the crown and wing-tip labels apart and put them in clear space with leader lines, and shorten the label text so nothing is clipped. Keep the tail long and clearly hanging from the lower corner (92761) down to the name-knot (92855), with the ribbon (92041) and name-strip (93506) branching from the knot.
